deities: Birni Devi (a local goddess of the Palampur area, worshipped as a form of Devi)

history.summary: Birni Devi Temple is a hilltop shrine dedicated to Mata Birni Devi, described by travel sources as the local deity of the Palampur region. The temple sits at about 2,200-2,240 m on the Dhauladhar slopes above Palampur and is reached by a moderate 3-5 hour trek via Lohna, Upper Bundla or Gallu Langha through pine and oak forest, offering panoramic views of the Kangra Valley and the Dhauladhar range. No dynasty, founder or built date is recorded in accessible sources, so the temple's age and origin remain undocumented. Coordinates used are the OpenStreetMap place-of-worship point (Mapcarta); a geocoder matched only a town-level point, so the POI position is preferred. Opening hours below are from a single aggregator and should be verified locally.

name: Birni Devi Temple
town_description: Palampur is a town in the Kangra Valley of Himachal Pradesh, set against the Dhauladhar range and known for its tea gardens (often called the Tea Capital of North India) and as a base for short treks.

travel.airport: Kangra Airport (Gaggal, DHM), about 40 km from Palampur.
travel.railway: Nearest major railhead: Pathankot (broad gauge), about 115 km away; the narrow-gauge Pathankot-Jogindernagar line serves stations in the valley.
travel.road: Well connected by road from Dharamshala (about 35 km), Pathankot and Shimla; the trek trailheads (Gallu Langha/Bundla) are a short drive from Palampur town.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to November, when the skies are clear and trekking conditions are best.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily by one aggregator (open-hours.in) - verify locally.
